topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture on cancer causation and states what students should learn.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can drive cancer evolution when cellular circumstances permit their accumulation and outgrowth.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence that environmental exposures influence cancer risk rather than cancer being solely a matter of bad luck.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma developing the argument through a detailed example.

topics.label: How environmental carcinogens damage DNA
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage that can become mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish initiating mutations from the promotional conditions that allow mutated cells to grow into tumours.

topics.label: Tissue and developmental specificity of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how susceptibility to carcinogens depends on the exposed tissue's circumstances and consolidate the preceding account of carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Investigating carcinogen exposure and carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence of carcinogenic effects is obtained and why establishing those effects remains difficult.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and the decisions made under uncertainty.
